summary: IllegalArgumentException when being attacked by a weak iron golem
description: The bug If an iron golem has high weakness level and if it hits you the game crashes. To reproduce - Spawn an iron golem - Give it weakness or strength effect lvl 2 or above - Hit it - Wait until it hits you Or spawn an iron golem using command: /summon iron_golem ~ ~ ~ {Attributes:[{Name:generic.AttackDamage,Base:0.0}]} and hit it Crash report 19w35a : [^crash-2019-08-30_16.15.51-server.txt] Description: Ticking entity java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: bound must be positive at java.base/java.util.Random.nextInt(Random.java:388) at asj.C(SourceFile:154) at aon.a(SourceFile:139) at aon.e(SourceFile:131) at apt.e(SourceFile:55) at java.base/java.util.stream.ForEachOps$ForEachOp$OfRef.accept(ForEachOps.java:183) at java.base/java.util.stream.ReferencePipeline$2$1.accept(ReferencePipeline.java:177) at java.base/java.util.Iterator.forEachRemaining(Iterator.java:133) at java.base/java.util.Spliterators$IteratorSpliterator.forEachRemaining(Spliterators.java:1801) at java.base/java.util.stream.AbstractPipeline.copyInto(AbstractPipeline.java:484) at java.base/java.util.stream.AbstractPipeline.wrapAndCopyInto(AbstractPipeline.java:474) at java.base/java.util.stream.ForEachOps$ForEachOp.evaluateSequential(ForEachOps.java:150) at java.base/java.util.stream.ForEachOps$ForEachOp$OfRef.evaluateSequential(ForEachOps.java:173) at java.base/java.util.stream.AbstractPipeline.evaluate(AbstractPipeline.java:234) at java.base/java.util.stream.ReferencePipeline.forEach(ReferencePipeline.java:497) at aof.a(SourceFile:80) at ajy.dh(SourceFile:623) at ajx.k(SourceFile:2275) at ajy.k(SourceFile:487) at asj.k(SourceFile:103) at ajx.h(SourceFile:2120) at ajy.h(SourceFile:294) at wj.a(SourceFile:596) at biv.a(SourceFile:656) at wj.a(SourceFile:399) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.b(SourceFile:836) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.a(SourceFile:775) at ebv.a(SourceFile:128) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.run(SourceFile:643) at java.base/java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:835)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Create a new Creative world with default settings.  
2. Open the chat and run the command ``/summon iron_golem ~ ~ ~`` to spawn an iron golem.  
3. Run the command ``/effect give @e[type=iron_golem,limit=1] minecraft:weakness 30 2`` to give the golem Weakness level 2 (or higher).  
4. Hit the iron golem with any weapon or item.  
5. Wait until the iron golem attacks you.  
6. Observe that the game crashes, producing an IllegalArgumentException (e.g., “bound must be positive”) in the crash report.
Observed Behavior: When an iron golem is given a Weakness or Strength effect of level two or higher and subsequently lands a melee hit on a player, the server crashes with an IllegalArgumentException. The crash occurs during the entity tick loop and is triggered by a call to java.util.Random.nextInt with a non‑positive bound, which produces the message “bound must be positive”. The stack trace shows the exception propagating through several internal classes before terminating the server thread. The problem can be reproduced by spawning a normal iron golem, applying either Weakness II or Strength II (or higher) using a potion, striking the golem, and then waiting for the golem’s attack to connect, or by summoning an iron golem with a zero attack‑damage attribute via the command /summon iron_golem ~ ~ ~ {Attributes:[{Name:"generic.AttackDamage",Base:0.0}]} and then hitting it. In both cases, when the golem’s attack lands the server generates a crash report similar to the one produced in snapshot 19w35a, containing the IllegalArgumentException and the full stack trace that ends with java.base/java.lang.Thread.run. This behavior is unexpected because the golem’s attack should simply deal damage, not cause a server‑side exception.
Expected Behavior: When an iron golem that has a Weakness or Strength potion effect level 2 or higher attacks a player, the attack should be processed normally—damage calculated according to the golem’s current attack‑damage attribute (including zero if overridden) and any applicable armor or effects—without causing the server to throw an IllegalArgumentException or terminate. The entity should remain alive and continue its normal AI behavior.
